teaser.text: UiPath sells software that turns work people do on computers into managed, automated processes. Its business is a loop: customers pay for software access and help, while UiPath spends to run, sell, support, and improve the platform.

stock.meta_description: UiPath stock forecast: bear, base and bull scenarios, cash conversion, customer expansion, AI adoption and valuation.
stock.opening: The weighted case for UiPath is $8.57 in October 2027, with the bear case at 30%, the base case at 55%, and the bull case at 15%. It hinges on better cash conversion, customer expansion and paid AI adoption.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains UiPath’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could UiPath's shares be in October 2027?

paragraphs.text: Weighted value is $8.57 in October 2027. That is a -38% return. The October 2029 weighted value is $12.32. That is a -10% return versus $13.72 today. The bear case has 30% probability; the base case has 55%. The bull case has 15%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for UiPath's stock forecast?

paragraphs.text: This is slower than the bull case, which produces $207.9 million initially and $450.5 million by the final date. It requires paid agents, stronger renewals and better delivery economics. The bear case falls to $37.2 million before recovering to $79.2 million, because weak expansion, services costs, stock pay and working-capital swings overwhelm modest revenue growth.

blocks.heading: How much cash does UiPath really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow was 371,208 in FY26. Capital spending was 19,048, leaving free cash flow of 352,160. The business needs little physical investment to add customers, but it still requires engineers, support staff, and hosting.

Stock pay was 290,676, leaving 61,484 under the memo’s “real free cash flow” measure. This is not a GAAP figure: issuing shares does not spend the same cash amount. It does, however, transfer part of the business to employees, so cash generation looks much thinner after including that cost.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for UiPath today?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio tells investors how many dollars they pay for each dollar of profit. UiPath’s trailing P/E is 20.5x, while its forward P/E is 17.4x. But net income includes interest earned on cash, and a $204.9 million release of a tax valuation allowance reduced reported tax expense without representing new software sales.

earnings.title: UiPath earnings: guidance and next results
earnings.meta_description: UiPath's next results are expected December 2, 2026; guidance points to growth, while revenue, profit and cash conversion are the key tests.
earnings.opening: UiPath's next results are expected on December 2, 2026. Watch whether revenue and ARR turn into operating profit and cash.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains UiPath's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has UiPath guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Revenue guidance is $1.789–$1.794 billion for the year to January 2027. ARR guidance is $2.065–$2.070 billion. Non-GAAP operating income guidance is $445 million. Adjusted free cash flow guidance is $425 million, and the FY2027 dilution ceiling is 0.0%.

blocks.heading: Did UiPath keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management’s promises also require the right comparison. Its initial public guidance for fiscal 2026 revenue was US$1.525 billion–US$1.530 billion, while reported revenue reached US$1.6106 billion. Revenue therefore exceeded that forecast, even though the internal growth target used for bonuses was not fully met. A favorable result against one promise does not prove success against another.

blocks.heading: What have UiPath's last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Revenue was 410,256, up from 361,728 in July 2025. GAAP operating income was 31,604, versus -20,185 a year earlier. This was the fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP operating profitability, which is stronger evidence than a single favorable contract-timing result.

Delivery economics were less encouraging. Gross margin fell to 80.4% from 82.2%. Stock compensation was about 45 million, while adjusted operating income was approximately 89 million. The gap shows why continuing GAAP improvement is the stricter test.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in UiPath's next results?

paragraphs.text: UiPath’s investor-relations calendar lists no upcoming event. The market’s provisional estimate is **December 2, 2026** for the third-quarter report, but UiPath has not confirmed it. Investors should compare revenue and ARR with guidance, then examine operating profit and cash collection. ARR matters only if customers renew and expand, and if those contracts eventually produce earnings and cash.
